### Also covered by

Riehl, *Category Theory in Context*, 2nd ed., §1.1, printed pp. 3-4 (PDF pp. 23-24); item `riehl:1.1:def-commute`.

Riehl defines commutativity for a category the same way Mac Lane does: two parallel directed paths of composable arrows commute when they have the same composite. The Chapter-1 coverage pass confirms this issue's `Commutative` predicate is still the only thing that would formalize it -- in-tree, commutativity is expressed either in the square special case (`Construction/Sq.v:47`, `dsq h u v k := k o u ~ v o h`) or ad hoc as an explicit `~` equation between two composites at each use site. No new obligation.

### Also covered by

Riehl §1.6, printed p. 39 (PDF p. 59); item `riehl:1.6:def-commutes`.

Riehl restates the definition in the diagram-chase section, this time explicitly over a quiver: a diagram is a quiver of morphisms in a category, and it commutes when any two paths with a common source and target have the same composite. That is exactly this issue's `Commutative` predicate over `Construction/Free/Quiver.v`'s `Quiver` (:54) and `FreeOnQuiver` (:431), with `Construction/Free.v`'s fold to composites. Coverage confirms no such definition is written anywhere, and that `Structure/Cone.v:24`'s `cone_coherence` and `Theory/Morphisms/Stability.v`'s `is_pullback_commutes` are shape-specific instances rather than the general predicate.

### Also covered by

Riehl §1.6 Lemma 1.6.20, printed p. 46 (PDF p. 66); item `riehl:1.6:lem20`.

Riehl proves that a faithful functor *reflects* commutativity: if the image of a diagram commutes then the diagram already commutes. This needs precisely the `Commutative` predicate this issue introduces, so it belongs here rather than in a separate issue. Coverage found `Theory/Functor.v:342` `Class Faithful` (field `fmap_inj`) and `Theory/Functor.v:106` `fmap_comp` present, but no composite/diagram-level restatement at all: the tree only ever applies `fmap_inj` inline, e.g. `Construction/ColouredPROP/LNL.v:251` `apply (@fmap_inj _ _ _ (@Comon_Forget_Faithful ...))` inside `LNL_lift_unique`.

Riehl §1.1 Remark 1.1.2, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 24); item `riehl:1.1:remark2`.

part: (vii) the category Measure of a.e.-classes of measurable maps
append_block:
### Also covered by

Riehl §1.1 Example 1.1.4 clause (vii), printed pp. 5-6 (PDF pp. 25-26); item `riehl:1.1:example4`.

Beyond the categories this issue and its siblings already track (clause (iii) preorders -> #223, (iv) finite ordinals and omega -> #224, (v) discrete categories -> #219, (vi) homotopy categories -> #260), Riehl's list of abstract categories includes one entry with no filed home: `Measure`, whose objects are measure spaces and whose morphisms are almost-everywhere-equivalence classes of measurable functions -- two parallel maps being identified when they differ on a null set. ### Also covered by

Riehl §1.1 Remark 1.1.5, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 26); item `riehl:1.1:remark5`.

Riehl's foundational remark is the same territory this issue maps: Russell's paradox forbids a set of all sets, which is why Definition 1.1.1 says "collection"; she then adopts the working convention of a countable tower of inaccessibles, so each stage is a Grothendieck universe one can enlarge as needed, rather than parametrizing definitions by universe levels. That is the *opposite* methodological choice from this library's, which is worth recording in the `docs/SIZE.md` this issue proposes. Coverage confirms `rg -i 'Grothendieck universe|inaccessible|V_kappa|proper class|Russell'` finds no universe axiom declared anywhere, and that `Instance/Cat.v:11,22-26` already explains that self-membership is blocked by universe polymorphism rather than by a size axiom.

- [ ] (from Riehl §1.1) `docs/SIZE.md` contrasts Riehl's Grothendieck-universe convention with the library's universe-polymorphism discipline explicitly, naming it as a deliberate divergence rather than an omission

### Also covered by

Riehl §1.1 Definition 1.1.6, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 27); item `riehl:1.1:def6`.

Riehl defines a *small* category as one with only a set's worth of arrows, and (via Remark 1.1.2) equivalently as the data of a set of objects, a set of morphisms, and `dom`, `cod`, `id` functions in Set with `dom` and `cod` retracting `id`. Chapter-1 coverage confirms `rg 'SmallCategory|Small_|IsSmall|LocallySmall'` returns no declaration: smallness is expressible only by choosing universe instantiations at definition sites, so it can appear neither as a hypothesis nor as a conclusion. The strongest place a hidden smallness quantifier could lurk was checked -- `Structure/Complete.v:115` reads `Definition Complete {C : Category} := forall (D : Category) (F : D --> C), Limit F`, quantifying over *all* categories at the ambient universe with no side condition. `Construction/Free/Quiver.v:398` `QuiverOfCat` supplies the objects-and-arrows-with-dom-and-cod half of Riehl's packaging but carries no identity selection.

- [ ] (from Riehl §1.1) Riehl's equivalent packaging of a small category as `(ob C, mor C, dom, cod, id)` with `dom` and `cod` retracting `id` -- i.e. the reflexive-quiver form, which the tree currently only approximates via `QuiverOfCat`

### Also covered by

Riehl §1.1 Definition 1.1.7, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 27); item `riehl:1.1:def7`.

Riehl defines *locally small* -- only a set's worth of morphisms between any pair of objects -- and immediately uses it to draw a distinction: none of the categories of her Example 1.1.3 is small, but each is locally small. Coverage confirms `rg -i 'LocallySmall'` returns 0 hits, so neither half of that sentence has an in-tree statement. ### Also covered by

Riehl §1.1, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 28); item `riehl:1.1:def-endomorphism`.

Riehl fixes the vocabulary in running prose: an endomorphism is a morphism whose domain equals its codomain, and an automorphism is an endomorphism that is an isomorphism -- which is exactly the `Aut` this issue builds, one level of generality up. Chapter-1 coverage confirms no `Definition`, `Class`, `Record` or `Notation` named `Endomorphism`, `Automorphism`, `End(-)` or `Aut(-)` exists anywhere (20 files mention "endomorphism", 8 mention "automorphism", all in comments). The *shape* is in tree and load-bearing -- `Theory/Morphisms.v:22` `Class Idempotent (f : x ~> x)`, `:32` `Class Involutive (f : x ~> x)`, and `Theory/Isomorphism.v:149` `iso_id : x ~= x` is literally an automorphism -- it is only unnamed.

Riehl §1.1 Example 1.1.11, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 28); item `riehl:1.1:example11`.

Riehl's five clauses are this issue's subject: isomorphisms in Set are the bijections; in groups, rings, fields and modules the bijective homomorphisms; in spaces the homeomorphisms, strictly stronger than bijective continuous maps; in the homotopy category the homotopy equivalences; and in a poset, antisymmetry forces the only isomorphisms to be identities. ### Also covered by

Riehl §1.6 Lemma 1.6.16, printed pp. 44-45 (PDF pp. 64-65); item `riehl:1.6:lem16`.
